# Psalm 108 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** A song. A psalm of David. My heart is confident, God! I will sing! I will make music with everything I've got!

**2** Wake up, harp and lyre! I'm going to wake up the dawn!

**3** I will thank you among the nations, LORD! I will sing your praises among the peoples!

**4** Your faithful love towers higher than the heavens; your reliability reaches to the clouds.

**5** Rise up above the heavens, God! Let your glory cover the whole earth!

**6** Rescue your beloved people! Save us with your powerful right hand and answer me!

**7** God has spoken from his sanctuary: 'I will celebrate as I divide up Shechem and measure out the Valley of Succoth.

**8** Gilead is mine, and Manasseh is mine. Ephraim is my helmet; Judah is my royal scepter.

**9** Moab is my washbowl; I'll toss my sandal over Edom; I'll shout in victory over Philistia!'

**10** Who will take me to the fortified city? Who will lead me into Edom?

**11** Haven't you rejected us, God? You no longer march out with our armies.

**12** Give us help against the enemy, because human help is worthless.

**13** With God we will fight and win — he's the one who will crush our enemies.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **108:2**: 'I'm going to wake up the dawn!' — one of the most energetic lines in the Psalms. David is so eager to praise that he'll start singing before the sun comes up.

- **108:12-13**: Human help is 'worthless' — but with God, 'we will fight and win.' The contrast is absolute. This isn't anti-human — it's recognizing where ultimate power lies.

— PNEUMA
